newsitem.title: UK: LME copper drifts, most others easier in reaction.
newsitem.headline: LME copper drifts, most others easier in reaction.

text.p: Copper prices edged lower on a lacklustre London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday, dragging most other base metals down with it.
The exception was nickel, which moved higher on continued institutional and fund buying interest.
"Copper ended down and has got a bit softer still since the kerb close. Everything else has tended to go the same way on the back of it," said one LME trader.
Three month copper futures finished the afternoon kerb at $1,927 a tonne, down $6 from Friday's afternoon kerb close. The market drifted further to $1,919/23 by 1645 GMT.
Spreads held steady, with cash moving to a premium of around $15 over three month values, little changed from Friday.
Some dealers said copper looked vulnerable to more losses.

"It's not looking too comfortable ahead of what is probably going to be another set of negative stock data (on Tuesday)," said one trader. A break below $1,900/10 support pointed to a drop to $1,880, he added.

European physical copper traders said business was still sluggish, although off-grade Russian demand had picked up on the back of the scrap supply tightness. Spot premiums were soft, reflecting slow demand for most grades.
If copper did fulfill its bearish technical potential, some traders were looking for losses in other metal markets, particularly lead and zinc.
Lead gave up early gains to finish just $0.50 higher at $810 while zinc edged back $1 to end at $1,033.
"We saw stale liquidation on lead and zinc," said a trader.
Nickel rallied $95 to $7,615, just $45 below key resisatance at $7,660. Physical business was generally quiet, but institutions and funds seemed keen to buy metal.
Tin was slow, losing $10 to $6,235 in line with the softer overall trend.
Aluminium weakened with copper, finishing at $1,477 from $1,484. The market looked vulnerable to a test of $1,470 support, below which further losses were expected, traders said.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,280/85 from $1,280.
